# NTP fluoride and cognition fixture

Fixture type: author-created paraphrase for deterministic testing.
Original source: https://doi.org/10.22427/NTP-MGRAPH-8
Publisher: U.S. National Toxicology Program
Published: 2024-08-21

NTP concluded with moderate confidence that higher fluoride exposure, such as
drinking-water concentrations above 1.5 mg/L, is associated with lower IQ in
children.

The review evaluated total fluoride exposure rather than community water
fluoridation alone. It found insufficient evidence to determine whether the
0.7 mg/L concentration recommended for U.S. community systems affects
children's IQ, and an association does not by itself establish causation.
